title: Research audit: quadratic dirty-interval amplification for commuting isometries
head: 519cf9b4f22a6a15f1af4b952f676e492b31a84e
body:
The sharp dirty-prefix coefficient does not transfer to a linear joint-interval bound, even with commuting scalar isometries and subset budget G=1. This package proves an all-height family in the unchanged PR628 reserved-depth word: at n=2^h, one chronological interval has target-row absolute sum floor(h²/2)+h+2, while every prefix/inverse prefix is bounded by h+2. Together with the existing squared-prefix upper bound, the worst interval growth is Θ(h²). The four-factor example gives 6>4 with full arbitrary-dirty restoration.

The result addresses PR1278/1295's explicit sharp-interval follow-up. It does not contradict their valid sufficient bounds or assert an actual rounded failure. Destination-supported errors can behave differently; the proof states that boundary explicitly. No production precision, supplier, selected record or kappa changes.

Only `research/dirty-interval-coefficient-boundary/` is added: complete proof and first counterexample in README, task/scope card, exact source pins, two checking representations, deterministic certificate, failure controls and registered replay. Base main is `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; coordination claim is [Discussion #1357](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1357). Final overlap refresh covers 843 open PRs and 93 Discussion records, complete pagination, without warnings.

Validation on macOS arm64:

- `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dirty-interval-coefficient-boundary` passes on CPython 3.12.14: 272,012 complete free-algebra intervals at n=1..16 in both signs; exact scalar attainment of every finite maximum; 87,380 literal family leaf events through h=8; independent recursive dense/Gauss-Jordan family checks through h=20; seven mathematical controls and six test groups.
- The separate literal scalar check enumerates all 510 sign assignments and 1,553,988 intervals at n=1..8. Full inverse-cut recurrence, actual source/receipt corruption and complete read-only relocation pass.
- Isolated optimized CPython 3.14.7 reproduces the same full mathematical receipt. Package metadata/provenance, `make selected-record-check` and patch whitespace pass.

The all-height conclusion rests on the written recurrence, not finite extrapolation. Hosted CI, full selected cold replay, numerical cyclic kernels, physical/compiler/hosting/caller admission and proof-assistant verification were not run for this local lemma.

Credit Chafik Boukhalfa (PR628/862/905), Hanson Sun (PR1085/1244), Charles Bethin (PR1278), Philipp/mightyOil (PR1295), Gareth Davidson (PR877), 0xkilgore (PR663) and retained lineage. Consumed heads are PR1085 `82b99c7d12dac009d35636562df4c6c91e885409`, PR1278 `06b8c006891ae78abe24b30d2fe9d8c188deafe8`, and unchanged PR628 `0768f97d06c623b8211e651543c66135796b62bf`; PR1295 `3a6773708f0d73f7dbee164f4c6e7658b0b41509` is the credited follow-up lead. PR1278 already published the n<=16 coefficient counts: this independently corroborates them and adds scalar norm attainments, with no priority claim for the counts. The new contribution is the all-height commuting-isometry lower family.

Prepared for Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, code, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; predecessor text and attribution retained. Separate algorithms are not independent human peer review. README/TASK give concrete next questions on destination-supported transport and the exact all-size constant.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
